newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-U.S. gasoline output record, refineries hum.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-U.S. gasoline output record, refineries hum.

text.p: There was a concensus among analysts on Tuesday's American Petroleum Institute weekly status report: "Bearish."
"The numbers are very bearish. We were expecting a five-million barrel build in crude and it was nearly doubled," said Richard Redash, oil market analyst at Prudential Securities.
The report, for the week ended May 30, showed crude stocks up a whopping 8.4 million barrels at just under 327 million barrels, even while refinery runs were up again sharply in the week.

Indeed, gasoline output last week hit a record 8.195 million barrels per day (bpd) as refinery runs rose 187,000 bpd to nearly 12.5 million bpd. That was on top of the previous week's 135,000 bpd rise in runs and put operating capacity nationwide at 98.4 percent -- 99.9 percent in "East of the Rockies" (PADD 1-4), or some 9.4 percentage points above the running rate in the same week last year.
"Clearly, operations are up pretty sharply here and we're seeing very high supply figures -- they look pretty bearish," said Thomas Blakeslee, an analyst at Cargill Investors Service.

Refineries are operating at a higher rate than last year even while refining capacity in the U.S. is 179,000 bpd higher, mainly because of the addition two weeks ago of Tosco Corp's Trainer, Pennsylvania plant.
"With crude runs humming along the way they are it suggests a lot more products are on the way," said Redash of Prudential.
"The refinery runs are higher than anything we have seen in a long time which is really bad for products," said Michael Busby, trader with Northville Industries in Melville, New York.
"You can see that by taking a look at the distillate number. This means heating oil, which is already out of season, may get badly hit," said Busby.
Distillate stocks rose just over five million barrels in the week to 107 million barrels, running about 11.5 million barrels above year-ago levels.

Gasoline stock were up nearly three million barrels at just under 200 million barrels, still almost seven million barrels lower than a year ago but narrowing the gap by a million barrels from the previous week.

Among other bearish data in the report: Crude imports were hardly changed and running just above 8.3 million bpd; Gasoline imports, though dropping back on the week, were still at about twice the previous year's rate at 437,000 bpd.

Some market participants said there might be solace in the fact that the crude stocks year-on-year fell back from more than 18 million barrels above last year's level to just under 14 million barrels. Also, from the fact that 5.5 million barrels of last week's crude build was in the volatile West Coast (PADD 5), while East Coast (PADD 1) stocks actually fell 1.3 million.
But most reckoned that would not be enough to change the generally bearish tenor of the report.

"We are definitely looking to go lower at the open tomorrow after we had big builds across the board. Although we have had an API reversal on Wednesday more often than not this year, if we are not above $20.00 by noon, we could close much lower on this," said Sal Gugliara of United Energy in New York.
In out-of-hours trading on ACCESS, crude futures for July delivery fell 32 cents on top of the regular session's 65-cent drop to stand at $20.01 a barrel.

July heating oil was down at 53.75/54.00 cents a gallon having dropped 1.70 cents to 54.62 cents in regular trading. Gasoline for July was down at another cent at 60.40/50 cents a gallon, having settled 1.55 cents lower at 61.44 cents.
